case_title: Shivaji Chintappa Patil v. State of Maharashtra
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 and sentenced to imprisonment for life
neutral_facts: The accused and the victim were married and had two children. The accused was addicted to liquor and had a history of abusing the victim, forcing her to get money from her mother. On the night of the incident, the accused and the victim went to sleep in their house. The next morning, the accused's brother called him to go to the field for harvesting crops. The accused informed him that the victim had committed suicide by hanging. The brother informed other relatives and the police. An advance death certificate was issued stating the cause of death as asphyxia due to strangulation. A post-mortem report was later conducted, which stated the cause of death as cardio respiratory arrest due to asphyxia due to hanging. The medical expert admitted that the rope found at the scene could have been used for suicidal hanging and that there were no marks on the body indicating violence or struggle. The prosecution relied on the accused's failure to explain the circumstances, but the courts found that the evidence was insufficient to prove the death was homicidal.
